events.what: White claims τ(H)≤6 for every 4-partite 4-uniform hypergraph with ν(H)=2, the case (r,ν)=(4,2) of Ryser's conjecture
events.ai_basis: The proof was found through four rounds of structured reasoning with GPT-5.6 Sol (OpenAI, model gpt-5.6-sol-pro) ... Every structural claim returned by the model was independently verified by the author's own exact computation

events.what: Domic & Gallardo give new sufficient conditions under which Ryser's conjecture holds

judgement.doubts: The White preprint is two weeks old, single-author and AI-generated; the verification described is the author's own MILP/enumeration checks, not expert reading. The record says it settles (4,2); whether computational checks cover an infinite class rigorously was not examined. Domic-Gallardo's conditions are unspecified in the record; coded none (sufficient conditions, no case settled) — could be case if the conditions define a natural class, but it would not change the status.

corrections.why: F1: the record itself says the preprint 'settles one case rather than the general r=4 conjecture' and coded it claimed only 'per §6.1's rule that a case settlement without expert digestion is claimed'. Scope is case (r,ν)=(4,2), so the tier is partial regardless of verification.

other: kept. The author states the proof 'was found through four rounds of structured reasoning with GPT-5.6 Sol' with the human verifying and correcting; that is generated. Doubt: the human caught two errors in the model's intermediate claims, so the line to assisted is close, and the account is the author's alone.
